tutorial.title: Discovering Types
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn about the different types of values we can store in variables.

lessons.title: Types
lessons.interactiveContent: We've already seen a few kinds of data like numbers and strings. In programming terms, these values are called types.

lessons.title: String
lessons.interactiveContent:
Strings are characters between quotes " ", like the value "High".

Make the variable sugar_content store the string value "High".

Make sure to pick "High".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Strings are characters between quotes " ", like the value "High".

Make the variable sugar_content store the string value "High".

Make sure to pick =, followed by "High".

lessons.title: Assigning
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we store a value, such as "High", in the variable sugar_content, we say that we assign the value to the variable.

Make sure to pick sugar_content, followed by =, and finally "High".
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we store a value, such as "High", in the variable sugar_content, we say that we assign the value to the variable.

Make sure to pick sugar_content, followed by =, and finally "High".

lessons.title: Integer
lessons.interactiveContent:
Integers are whole numbers without decimal places, such as 42.

Assign a number without quotation marks to make the variable store an integer value.

Make sure to pick 42.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Integers are whole numbers without decimal places, such as 42.

Assign a number without quotation marks to make the variable store an integer value.

Make sure to pick =, followed by 42.

lessons.title: Float
lessons.interactiveContent:
Floats describe floating-point numbers with one or more decimal places after a point, like 3.14159.

Assign a decimal number to pi so that it stores a floating-point value rather than a string or integer.

Make sure to pick 3.14159.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Floats describe floating-point numbers with one or more decimal places after a point, like 3.14159.

Assign a decimal number to pi so that it stores a floating-point value rather than a string or integer.

Make sure to pick =, followed by 3.14159.

lessons.title: Booleans
lessons.interactiveContent:
The boolean type has only two possible values: True and False. We write them without quotation marks.

Store the value True inside the received_newsletter variable.

Make sure to pick True.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The boolean type has only two possible values: True and False. We write them without quotation marks.

Store the value True inside the received_newsletter variable.

Make sure to pick =, followed by True.

lessons.title: Basic data types I
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've seen the basic data types in Python - strings, integers, floats, and booleans.

If we are unsure of a value type, we can check it! Here, type() checks that is_ready is a bool, which is short for boolean.

Make sure to pick type.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We've seen the basic data types in Python - strings, integers, floats, and booleans.

You can check a value's type with type(). Here, bool is short for boolean.

Complete the call to display the type of is_ready.

Make sure to pick type.

lessons.title: Basic data types II
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can get a variable's type using type() with the variable name. By adding print(), we can see the variable type in the console.

Make sure to pick type followed by (fuel_deposit) and then (, ), print.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can get a variable's type using type() with the variable name. By adding print(), we can see the variable type in the console.

Make sure to pick type, followed by (fuel_deposit), (, ), and finally print.

lessons.title: int()
lessons.interactiveContent:
Python has built-in functions to convert data types. For example, int() helps us convert the age variable's string value to an integer.

Make sure to pick int(age).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Python has built-in functions to convert data types. int() converts a numeric string to an integer.

Convert age from a string to an integer so the last line prints True.

Make sure to pick int(age).

lessons.title: str()
lessons.interactiveContent:
The str() function allows us to take numerical values and convert them to strings.

Convert the password variable to a string to compare it to the old password.

Make sure to pick str followed by ( and then password, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
The str() function allows us to take numerical values and convert them to strings.

Convert the password variable to a string so it can be compared to the old password.

Make sure to pick str, followed by (, password, and finally ).

lessons.title: int(float) doesn't round
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we use int() on a float value, we'll simply remove the decimal point and subsequent values. There will be no rounding.

Make sure to pick int.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we use int() on a float value, we'll simply remove the decimal point and subsequent values. There will be no rounding.

Convert price so the line prints 9, cutting off everything after the point.

Make sure to pick int.

lessons.title: float()
lessons.interactiveContent:
Likewise, we can use float() on an integer. This will add a decimal point, and the ability to store fractional values.

Make sure to pick float followed by ( and then weeks, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Likewise, we can use float() on an integer. This will add a decimal point, and the ability to store fractional values.

Convert weeks so the line prints 12.0 with a decimal point added.

Make sure to pick float, followed by (, weeks, and finally ).

lessons.title: int(bool)
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we use int() on a boolean, the equivalent numerical value will be 1 for True and 0 for False.

Convert member and not_member to integers to check their new boolean values.

Make sure to pick int, followed by int.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we use int() on a boolean, the equivalent numerical value will be 1 for True and 0 for False.

Convert member and not_member into whole numbers so the lines print 1 and 0.

Make sure to pick int, followed by int.

lessons.title: bool()
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use bool() to convert a variable into a Boolean. If the variable has content, it will become True. If it's empty or 0, it'll become False.

Convert these variables into booleans, and check the output.

Make sure to pick bool(member) followed by bool(middle_name) and then bool(foot_size), bool(siblings).
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can use bool() to convert a variable into a boolean.

A value with content becomes True. An empty value or 0 becomes False.

Convert each value to a boolean. Store each conversion in the variable with the matching name.

Make sure to pick bool(member), followed by bool(middle_name), bool(foot_size), and finally bool(siblings).

lessons.hardModeContent:
